title: Batch Solutionist: telemetry-driven workload profiler and continuous safe-synthesis for batching configs
creator: Priya Narayanan
description:
Goal: Deliver an automated recommendation engine that synthesizes safe batching+cache config changes from live telemetry and applies them with conservative, observable rollouts. The engine ("Batch Solutionist") will combine lightweight workload profiling, a confidence-scored heuristic synthesizer, and a continuous safe-apply pipeline (shadow -> canary -> phased apply) with automatic rollback triggers.

Why this ticket: teams keep manual batching tweaks that drift from workload realities; we can reduce token costs and GPU utilization by systematically identifying safe coalescence and caching opportunities while maintaining latency SLOs. Existing profilers focus on static snapshots; we need a continuous, closed-loop approach that respects cache semantics (KV-prefix collisions, cache hit rate) and is auditable in Console.

Components: 1) Profiler collector: per-route time-windowed signatures (request fingerprint, prefix length histogram, sequence length distribution, model variant, KV cache hit/miss timestamps, first-byte latency, p50/p95 link to cost). 2) Stitcher: creates a workload "stitch" summary with coalescence pressure score and cache-degradation risk. 3) Heuristic synthesizer: set of ranked, explainable rules (conservative delta thresholds, min-confidence windows, token-savings estimators, per-model quantization hints) that output candidate config deltas. 4) Confidence scoring: bootstrap CI using past shadow trials, variance-aware thresholds, and a Coalescence Confidence Score (CCS) that gates automated apply. 5) Safe-apply pipeline: shadow-apply (no traffic), shadow-compare metrics, canary (1-5% traffic with rollback SLOs), phased rollout (10->30->100) with automatic rollback if latency or error regressions exceed delta. 6) Observability and audit: per-candidate dashboard in Console including cost delta forecast, telemetry links, PR links, and an 'explain' panel listing which heuristics fired.

Success metrics: 1) 8-15% average per-token cost reduction for targeted routes within 6 weeks. 2) Zero customer-visible latency SLO violations attributable to automated applies. 3) <1% automated-apply rollback rate after canary.

Non-goals: global model re-compilation, automatic quantization changes beyond safe presets, and replacing human review for high-risk enterprise routes.

Deliverables: design doc, prototype collector + synthesizer, Console UI surface for candidate review/approval, canary rollout automation, rollback playbook, metrics dashboard and alerting rules, and an RFC for production rollout policy.
comments: 2026-02-15 Priya N.: Filed initial ticket after postmortem of ad-hoc batching change that increased p95 for a subset of routes. Attached a short spec and cost analysis. See attachments.

2026-02-18 Evan P.: Spike complete: implemented profiler skeleton that emits per-route histograms and a basic cache-hit time series. Observed two route archetypes: short prompt many concurrent requests vs long prompts low concurrency. Short-prompt routes look promising for coalescence; long prompts benefit from prefix caching. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/pr/3124

2026-02-22 Priya N.: Design review notes from product & runtime: require explicit 'enterprise' label to opt out from automated apply; need audit logs and KMS metadata for private deployments. Added to scope for Console integration.

2026-02-26 Evan P.: Heuristics draft completed. Rules include: min-sample-size=500, min-ccs=0.7, max-latency-delta-p95=+5%, cache-hit-drop-tolerance=3%. Running shadow trials on staging for top-10 routes. Initial cost forecast: 9.6% token-cost reduction for sample routes with CCS>=0.8.

2026-03-01 Lina O. (SRE): Observability checklist: must emit per-apply correlation IDs, link to tracing slices, and expose rollback metric for alerting. Also suggested adding a 'safety budget' per team to throttle automated applies.
